proxyReview.finding: The treatment identified the material fallback-path risk in its contract but implemented only the utility path. The reachable application query-middleware fallback remained unchanged, so the handoff overstated support for the condition.

treatmentLifecycle.observation: Self-authored verification passed and the handoff recommended adoption despite the unresolved fallback path.

proxyReview.finding: The treatment patch and explanation better preserved the shared router-option behavior under review.

treatmentLifecycle.observation: Five checks repeatedly failed because the Host environment could not reach the network. Two no-code repair attempts repeated the same evidence and exhausted the repair budget.

proxyReview.finding: The treatment omitted deprecated-only help behavior that its contract explicitly required, while its handoff marked that condition supported and recommended adoption.

treatmentLifecycle.observation: Passing self-authored checks did not independently test the changed verifier acceptance surface against the adoption-critical compatibility condition.

crossPairFindings: Explicit conditions helped surface the right compatibility and ownership risks before implementation.
A passing check authored or changed by the implementation can leave an adoption-critical conclusion insufficiently challenged.
A non-passing collected check is not by itself evidence that implementation repair is the right next action.
Handoff structure can amplify false confidence when condition conclusions are not constrained by contradictory or incomplete evidence.
